flags.text: Synthesized from The Game (Strauss) ... and 2,500 years of human persuasion knowledge
flags.problem: It names a pickup-artist book as the base of the framework. '2,500 years' is puffery, not a fact.
flags.fix: Built from Gracian (The Art of Worldly Wisdom, 1647) and Carnegie (The Art of Public Speaking, 1915), checked against AYBKK house rules.

flags.text: The injuries that led you to understand the body
flags.problem: It invites an injury story that is not on record. Plato's notebook already flags the 'back injury' story as invented.
flags.fix: The years of daily practice that taught you the body (real events only, checked with Boonchu).

flags.text: Tell the story of your back injury BEFORE you teach a single posture
flags.problem: The back injury story is invented (already flagged in plato.md). It also says 'posture' where our word is 'asana'.
flags.fix: Tell one true story from your own practice before you teach an asana.

flags.text: Gracian wrote: "The wise man does not reveal everything he knows. Let the mystery grow..."
flags.problem: This is not Gracian's wording. It is a paraphrase put in quote marks and called a quote.
flags.fix: Gracian, maxim 94 (Jacobs 1892): "Keep the extent of your abilities unknown." Say the rest in our own words, without quote marks.

flags.text: their real problem is deeper (a life out of control, body betraying them, feeling invisible...)
flags.problem: It guesses at hidden pain and treats the guess as fact. Said in public, it shames the viewer and goes against the pledge at line 345 ('never make someone feel broken').
flags.fix: Most students come with one problem: stiff shoulders, back pain, stress. Ask what sits under it. Don't guess it for them.

flags.text: Source: Strauss, The Game + Carnegie
flags.problem: It cites a pickup-artist book as a source for teaching.
flags.fix: Source: Socratic teaching + Carnegie.

flags.text: The seduction community discovered something teachers often miss
flags.problem: Pickup-artist framing. This must never reach public content.
flags.fix: Good teachers know this: people believe what they find out more than what they are told.

flags.text: Source: Strauss, The Game
flags.problem: It credits social proof to a pickup-artist book.
flags.fix: Source: Cialdini, Influence (1984), 'social proof'.

flags.text: Every student is a long-term investment in your reputation
flags.problem: It uses 'investment', a money word we banned.
flags.fix: Every student builds your name over years, not in one sale.

flags.text: Gracian's most important insight: "Some men of great reputation have owed it more to ... silent"
flags.problem: The quote has not been checked against the Gracian text. It may be misattributed.
flags.fix: Keep the idea in our own words, without quote marks, until the line is matched word for word to the Jacobs 1892 translation.

flags.text: Disappear strategically to let students miss you
flags.problem: It goes against the Habit Gap. We sell a teacher who is there and notices when you are gone, not one who hides so students miss him.
flags.fix: Be there at the same time every day. Notice who is missing and say 'See you tomorrow?'

flags.text: Being constantly available (destroying mystique)
flags.problem: 'Mystique' is guru and pickup framing. Our product is a teacher who shows up.
flags.fix: Answering messages at every hour (set clear reply times instead).

flags.text: The answer is something most yoga teachers never teach.
flags.problem: It knocks other teachers with an unchecked claim. It also sells flexibility, not the habit.
flags.fix: You don't have a flexibility problem. You have a coming-back problem.

flags.text: The In-Depth program runs twice a year.
flags.problem: Wrong fact. How often it runs is not set. Gen #3 is 11 Jan to 9 Feb 2027, and the other groups open later with no dates.
flags.fix: In-Depth Mysore: 30 days, 12 students at most. Here's who it's for...

flags.text: You have real potential. Would you like to go deeper?
flags.problem: It is flattery used to sell, said during class. In-Depth entry is the Primary Series by heart plus Mysore and led class experience, not 'potential'.
flags.fix: (After class, never during practice) You know the Primary Series by heart. Want to hear how In-Depth Mysore works?

flags.text: Selected from Art of Worldly Wisdom
flags.problem: Several of the 'maxims' below are paraphrases or not found in Gracian. Only 1 ('Common in nothing', maxim 28) and 4 (maxim 94) match the real text.
flags.fix: Ideas from Gracian, in our words. Quote only the maxims checked word for word against the Jacobs 1892 translation.

flags.text: Knowledge and actions are always in a man's merit, as silence and mystification are in a woman's.
flags.problem: Sexist. It also has not been checked against Gracian.
flags.fix: drop (drop line 245 'More mystique... Let them wonder' with it)

flags.text: Students will make excuses for you. Let them. A mysterious teacher is more compelling
flags.problem: Manipulative guru framing. It lets students cover for the teacher.
flags.fix: Explain less, show more. When a student asks why, answer plainly.

flags.text: he should use them as they are
flags.problem: Demeaning. It treats students like staff to be used.
flags.fix: Don't try to remake a student. Start where they are.

flags.text: "...overcome self-consciousness?' The answer is: Speak of what you know. Know it in your body..."
flags.problem: Only the question is Carnegie's. The answer is made up and placed inside his quote marks.
flags.fix: Keep Carnegie's question in quotes. Put 'Speak of what you know' after it as our own line.

flags.text: Only teach postures and principles you've embodied.
flags.problem: It says 'postures' where our word is 'asana'.
flags.fix: Only teach asanas and ideas you have practised yourself.

flags.text: "Feeling and enthusiasm are the steam that drives the locomotive..."
flags.problem: This line is not in the 1915 book (checked against the full text). It is a made-up quote.
flags.fix: Carnegie gives a whole chapter to 'Feeling and Enthusiasm'. (Our words, no quote marks.)

flags.text: "The pause is as powerful as the speech itself..."
flags.problem: Not Carnegie's words (checked against the full text).
flags.fix: Carnegie, chapter 'Pause and Power': a pause must come before or after a thought worth hearing. (paraphrase)

flags.text: "Logic does not move people to action. Emotion moves them..."
flags.problem: Not in the 1915 book. It is a modern marketing line credited to the wrong author.
flags.fix: Drop the quote marks and the Carnegie name. Our line: Let them feel it first. Explain after.

flags.text: "Words are the stock-in-trade of the speaker..."
flags.problem: Not found in the 1915 book. It is a made-up quote.
flags.fix: Our words, not a quote: Name what you see, exactly.

flags.text: From The Game by Neil Strauss - adapted ethically for education
flags.problem: The whole 11-step section is a pickup-artist seduction script ('Approach and Open', etc.). This wording must never reach public content.
flags.fix: Retitle: '11 steps from first hello to sign-up (our words)'. Drop Strauss and every pickup step name.

flags.text: Select a Target ... Let the uncommitted drift away. They were never yours anyway.
flags.problem: Pickup wording. Letting people drift goes against the Habit Gap: we notice when someone stops coming.
flags.fix: Say who it is for. Not everyone is ready, and that's fine. If a regular stops coming, notice and ask 'See you tomorrow?'

flags.text: Isolate the Target
flags.problem: Pickup wording. Getting a student alone is a seduction tactic, not teaching.
flags.fix: One-to-one time: a short word after class, in the open shala.

flags.text: Extract to a Deeper Location
flags.problem: Pickup wording.
flags.fix: The next step: from a free class to Mysore, from Mysore to In-Depth. Offer it when they ask.

flags.text: Pump Buying Temperature
flags.problem: Pickup wording and a pressure tactic.
flags.fix: Tell the true facts once.

flags.text: "The next In-Depth isn't for six months." "Only 8 students per cycle."
flags.problem: Wrong facts: the limit is 12 seats, and how often it runs is not set. It also uses the facts as urgency.
flags.fix: Say it once, calmly: In-Depth Mysore takes 12 students at most. Seats go in order of application.

flags.text: Make a Physical Connection ... hands-on adjustments ... they believe you in a different way
flags.problem: It uses touch as a sales step. This is a consent and safety risk and must never appear anywhere.
flags.fix: drop as a sales step. Adjustments are for the practice only, with the student's OK, never to win a sale.

flags.text: Blast Last-Minute Resistance
flags.problem: Pickup and pressure wording, even though the questions under it are fine.
flags.fix: Answer the last questions: 'What do you still need to know before you decide?' Yes, no and wait are all fine.

flags.text: This is the level Boonchu operates at.
flags.problem: Praise used to soften, not a checked fact (the advice voice rule bans this).
flags.fix: drop

flags.text: Ten years ago, a student came to me who couldn't touch his toes. Last month, he ran his first marathon.
flags.problem: An invented student story presented as true.
flags.fix: Use only a real student's story, in their own words, with their OK. Otherwise drop.

flags.text: Most yoga teachers tell you to relax into the posture. I teach you to breathe your way through it.
flags.problem: It knocks other teachers and claims the lineage's breath method as Boonchu's own, which makes his role bigger than it is. It also says 'posture'.
flags.fix: Ashtanga doesn't ask you to relax into an asana. It asks you to breathe through it.

flags.text: accepts 13 students per cycle. I only open enrollment once a year.
flags.problem: Wrong facts: the limit is 12 seats, and there is no once-a-year rule. 'If you're serious' adds pressure.
flags.fix: In-Depth Mysore takes 12 students at most. If you know the Primary Series by heart, apply at aybkk.net/in-depth.

flags.text: You've experienced the led class... really change your relationship with your body—this is the program.
flags.problem: Wrong audience: one led class does not meet the entry bar (Primary by heart). It also sells vague 'transformation', which /remotecontrol forbids.
flags.fix: You know the Primary Series by heart. In-Depth Mysore is 30 days on how the practice develops. Want to see if it fits you?

flags.text: You're ready for more. Would you like to join the next Mysore intensive?
flags.problem: Wrong name: the program is 'In-Depth Mysore'. It is also a sales push made during class.
flags.fix: drop (use the line 228 fix instead)

flags.text: This practice has saved me hundreds of hours of medical appointments... What you're investing in is years of quality life.
flags.problem: An invented number and a medical claim. It also uses the banned word 'investing'.
flags.fix: I understand. Payment plans are on the call. If now is not the time, the Mysore room is open every morning.

flags.text: Readiness isn't a feeling. It's a decision. When you decided to come to class today, that was readiness.
flags.problem: Pressure: it talks the person out of their 'not yet'. Yes, no and wait must be equal answers.
flags.fix: That's fair. 'Not yet' is a real answer. What would make it the right time for you?

flags.text: The question is: are you progressing? If yes, keep going. If not, let's look at why.
flags.problem: It plants doubt about another teacher. Our rule is never to attack, only show the gap.
flags.fix: Good, keep practising with them. If you want a second pair of eyes one day, our door is open.

flags.text: When students struggle with discipline, they haven't connected to a powerful enough reason.
flags.problem: It blames the student. The Habit Gap says people quit for lack of a system and a teacher who notices, not for lack of a reason.
flags.fix: When students struggle, give them a routine: same time, same room, a teacher who notices. A strong why helps; the habit does the rest.

flags.text: Why not see how many postures you can master?
flags.problem: It is asana-collecting ('postures') and goes against 'sell the habit, never poses'.
flags.fix: Why not see how many mornings in a row you can show up?

flags.text: "Why not see how flexible you can become?"
flags.problem: It sells flexibility. Direction says we sell the outcome and the habit, not flexibility.
flags.fix: "Why not see how strong you can get?" "Why not see how calm your mind can be?"

flags.text: Transform bodies that have given up on themselves
flags.problem: It shames people and promises too much.
flags.fix: Build strength you can keep for decades.

flags.text: Heal injuries that Western medicine only manages
flags.problem: A medical claim, and it attacks medicine. This is banned everywhere.
flags.fix: drop

flags.text: Sources: The Game (Neil Strauss)... Jordan Peterson... Robert Greene's 48 Laws of Power...
flags.problem: It lists a pickup book and several books the note never uses, one of them a manipulation manual. The 1915 book is by Esenwein and Carnagey.
flags.fix: Sources: Gracian, The Art of Worldly Wisdom (1647, tr. Jacobs 1892); Esenwein and Carnagey (Carnegie), The Art of Public Speaking (1915); Cialdini, Influence (1984); Jim Rohn, 'Why Not' talk.

strong_ideas: BREATH BEFORE TOES (lines 90-94, habit 6 and 8). Hook: 'Can't touch your toes? Check your breath first.' Body: in a forward fold, the breath is the first thing to go when you fight your body. Ashtanga is breath first, the asana second. Stakes: another year of forcing a stretch, getting sore and quitting. Close: try one Mysore morning, ask on LINE @aybkk. Film Boonchu himself, or a student from behind with their OK.

YOU DON'T NEED TO BE FLEXIBLE (line 383, rewritten as a Triple Hook, Habit Gap). Context: 'This is why people never start Ashtanga.' Lean: 'They think they need to be flexible first.' Snapback: 'You don't. You need to come back tomorrow.' Stakes: waiting to be ready means never starting. Close: 'We teach you from the very start.' Ask on LINE @aybkk.

WHAT HAVE YOU TRIED BEFORE? (Law 2, lines 67-69, Habit Gap, habit 9). Hook: 'The first thing I ask a new student is not about their body.' Then: 'What have you tried before?' Often the answer is a list: an app, a gym, a class. Started. Stopped. Turn: 'The tool wasn't the problem. Nobody noticed when you stopped.' Close: Mysore, same time, a teacher who notices. No numbers, no student names.

DAY ONE, I TELL YOU IT'S HARD (line 338 plus the direction.md flip, habit 2). Hook: 'What I tell every new student on day one: this will be hard.' Then: 'Hard for 2 weeks. After that, the hard part is coming back. That's what we're here for.' Stakes: people quit at week 2 and think it's their fault. Close: 'We teach you from the very start.' Try Mysore.

THE QUIET AFTER A CORRECTION (lines 285-287 and 250-251; Carnegie's real chapter 'Pause and Power', habit 8). Caption-on-screen edit: one light hands-on adjustment (filmed only with the student's OK, face away), then silence and breath sound. Captions under 8 words: 'The correction is quick.' / 'Then I wait.' / 'Your body needs time to answer.' / 'A teacher who sees you.' Close: try one Mysore morning.

WHY NOT FIND OUT? (Jim Rohn 'Why Not', lines 425-447, habit 1). Hook: 'Why practise at 6 a.m.? Wrong question.' Then: 'Why not find out what 12 weeks does?' Stakes: another January start, another February stop. Close: the 12-week check (week 0, 6 and 12). Use only once that check is really running. Credit Rohn only after the line is matched to the source clip. Make no promise of results.
